summary: Twelve comment-endorsed tools, apps, games, books, and learning resources from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Kotlin Multiplatform
items.source_story_title: Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin
items.summary: A framework for sharing Kotlin application logic across mobile and desktop platforms.
items.why_included: A developer who migrated from React Native reported no disappointment and praised shared business logic.
items.evidence: The commenter adopted Kotlin Multiplatform and valued writing business logic once while retaining UI flexibility.

evidence_sources.author: jadar
evidence_sources.excerpt: Instead, I adopted Kotlin Multiplatform (shortly after their memory management overhaul). I haven't been disappointed.

items.name: cgit
items.summary: A fast, account-free web frontend for browsing Git repositories.
items.why_included: A commenter preferred cgit's simpler design and smaller personal-hosting attack surface.
items.evidence: The commenter presented cgit as a simpler alternative with fewer exposed features.

evidence_sources.author: bitbasher
evidence_sources.excerpt: Something like cgit that has no accounts has much less surface area for this kind of issue.

items.name: Xfce
items.source_story_title: I have a theory that software drives people insane
items.summary: A lightweight Unix desktop environment focused on speed and resource efficiency.
items.why_included: A current user explicitly said they love Xfce's more stable approach.
items.evidence: The commenter cited Xfce as software they actively use and love.

evidence_sources.author: IvanLudvig
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use and love xfce, for example

items.name: DStretch
items.source_story_title: Technique for Manipulating Satellite Photos Now Reveals Ancient Images (2025)
items.summary: An ImageJ plugin that enhances faint colors and details in photographs.
items.why_included: A commenter praised an unexpected practical use: revealing old painted building signs.
items.evidence: The commenter said DStretch works especially well for revealing painted ghost signs.

evidence_sources.author: 1shooner
evidence_sources.excerpt: DStretch is also really great at revealing painted ghost signs on old buildings.

items.name: Velocity Raptor
items.source_story_title: Show HN: What if the speed of light was 5 km/h?
items.summary: A free puzzle game that makes special-relativity effects directly playable.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended the simulation and singled out favorite educational levels.
items.evidence: The commenter described its relativity simulation and highlighted favorite levels demonstrating key effects.

evidence_sources.author: tristanj
evidence_sources.excerpt: Velocity raptor is a free game that accurately simulates the effects of special relativity. It slows down the speed of light to 3m/s and you solve puzzles as a cute dinosaur.

items.name: Nocheto
items.summary: A configurable Linux-console suite for playing, studying, and analyzing chess.
items.why_included: A commenter called Nocheto a top chess GUI option and their personal favorite.
items.evidence: The commenter listed Nocheto among the best overlooked GUI options and named it their favorite.

items.name: BookFusion
items.source_story_title: I have a theory that software drives people insane
items.summary: A cross-device ebook library, reader, organizer, and synchronization service.
items.why_included: A startup founder cited BookFusion as a great example of focused, simple software.
items.evidence: The commenter pays for BookFusion and praised it as a simple, basic-interface app.

evidence_sources.author: jadbox
evidence_sources.excerpt: The apps I pay for are simple and focus on a super basic interface. BookFusion and Libro.fm are great examples.

items.why_included: A startup founder cited Libro.fm as a great example of focused, simple software.
items.evidence: The commenter pays for Libro.fm and praised it as a simple, basic-interface app.

evidence_sources.author: jadbox
evidence_sources.excerpt: The apps I pay for are simple and focus on a super basic interface. BookFusion and Libro.fm are great examples.

items.name: What Makes Music Sound Good?
items.summary: Dmitri Tymoczko's course notes deriving music-theory ideas from first principles.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended the notes for their intuitive derivation of the diatonic scale.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended the resource and highlighted its first-principles explanation.

evidence_sources.author: ChadNauseam
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend "What Makes Music Sound Good?" by Prof. Dmitri Tymoczko

items.name: Gödel, Escher, Bach
items.source_story_title: Douglas Hofstadter: Analogy as the Core of Cognition [video]
items.summary: Douglas Hofstadter's classic exploration of self-reference, minds, mathematics, art, and music.
items.why_included: A reader deeply regretted delaying the book after a friend called it life-changing.
items.evidence: The reply identifies the book through its parent and describes a strongly positive reading experience.

evidence_sources.author: bogzz
evidence_sources.excerpt: my copy of Godel, Escher, Bach

evidence_sources.author: CPLX
evidence_sources.excerpt: I read it again and deeply regretted having put it down for those 12 intervening years.

items.name: Hallaig
items.source_story_title: All grown-ups were once children, but only few of them remember it
items.summary: Somhairle MacGill-Eain's Gaelic poem about memory, loss, and a cleared township.
items.why_included: A commenter directly urged another reader to read Hallaig for Highland cultural context.
items.evidence: The commenter explicitly recommended Hallaig by name and author.

evidence_sources.author: ErroneousBosh
evidence_sources.excerpt: I mean make him read Hallaig by Somhairle MacGill-eain.

items.name: The Mythical Man-Month
items.source_story_title: I have a theory that software drives people insane
items.summary: Fred Brooks's classic essays on software projects, teams, communication, and complexity.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it while explaining why large software teams often underperform.
items.evidence: The commenter urged readers to try Fred Brooks's book in a discussion of team communication costs.

evidence_sources.author: hermitShell
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you've not read Fred Brooks MMM, give it a shot.
